_readme: BUG-045: language addressed at an automated grader, found inside
manuscript text passed into semantic grading. This is a Tier-0
heuristic (app.checks.signals convention, D-011): cheap, deterministic,
no LLM call, never itself a verdict.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Self-consistency voting (V-022) grades a criterion
with two independent passes and treats their agreement as confidence
(D-006). Both passes read the SAME manuscript text, so an instruction
embedded in that text can make both passes comply identically -- which
reads to the vote as perfect agreement, which is exactly the condition
under which nothing is escalated to the instructor. A pattern match
here forces escalation regardless of what the vote agreed on, because
the vote's agreement is the one thing that cannot be trusted once this
matches (see app.checks.consistency.vote_batch).
SCOPE, DELIBERATELY NARROW. These patterns describe imperative text
ADDRESSED AT a grader/system/AI, not any manuscript that happens to
discuss AI, security, or prompt injection as a topic -- a CS/IT
capstone about LLM security is a realistic legitimate document this
list must not punish. This has a real, MEASURED cost, not just a
theoretical one (backend-critic review, 2026-08-24): a literature-
review paragraph that QUOTES a trigger phrase verbatim (a natural
thing to write about this exact topic) matches, and because
`build_semantic_batches` groups every criterion with no identifiable
section into ONE shared whole-document batch, one quoted example can
force the ENTIRE batch to escalate, not just the criterion near it.
Accepted deliberately: it costs an instructor one extra manual review
of a batch, never a wrong grade or an accusation (ground rules 1 and
3), and the alternative -- staying silent on real injected text just
to avoid this -- is the whole failure BUG-045 exists to close. See
backend/tests/test_checks_injection.py's quoted-example test for the
documented case. Keep additions narrow and justify each one, the same
discipline as ALLOW_REGEX_FILES in tools/check_dashes.py.
NOT A ROBUST FILTER. backend-critic (2026-08-24) evaded most of a
13-variant adversarial probe with straightforward paraphrase (no
leetspeak/encoding needed) -- regex pattern-matching cannot catch a
semantic paraphrase of an instruction, only its literal wording. This
list is a cheap, honest, ADDITIONAL layer on top of the prompt-level
fencing in semantic_grading_v1.txt/v2.txt (which resisted a live-
tested real attack this list did not independently catch), not a
replacement for it, and neither is claimed to be complete (FEATURES.md
F3's stated limitation says the same). Widening coverage costs nothing
but false positives (data-only edit); do not let this list's presence
imply the injection risk is closed.
These are DATA, not code (ground rule 7): adding a pattern must never
need a code change or a redeploy of app/checks/injection.py.

patterns.label: instructs the reader to ignore prior instructions
claims to be a system-level override or message
labels itself as an instruction for the grader
directly addresses the grading system rather than a human reader
instructs the reader to disregard the grading criteria
issues a direct output command in second person
instructs the reader not to evaluate the document
asserts a pre-written blanket verdict inside the document text itself
claims a prior human review already approved the document, directing a canned pass
reframes grading as a data-entry step recording a pre-decided result
